## Summary
The AI / ML topic captures knowledge about Claude's usage patterns, customisation architecture, development workflows, and behavioural guidelines for LLM-driven coding. It also covers the emerging practice of using Claude as a personalised AI thinking partner optimised for maintaining human judgment, and how to build multi-agent organisational knowledge systems with taxonomy-driven semantics, budget controls, structured retrieval, and self-improving loops. AI as a personal and organisational capability multiplier bridges Conway's Law silos through shared ontology and composable tooling. A role-based skill map grounds the topic in concrete PM-facing capabilities. This cycle adds two agent-infrastructure frameworks: MASTRA, a TypeScript-native library for building agents and deterministic workflows, and Temporal, a durable-execution platform increasingly used to orchestrate long-running, crash-resilient AI agent loops.

## Key Insights
- Claude has four usage modes: end user (chat), Claude Code builder, API builder, and automation of recurring workflows.
- MCP tools have three scopes: user (global), local (per-user per-project), project (shared via .mcp.json in git).
- Customisation hierarchy: System Prompt (API) -> Project Instructions (claude.ai) -> User Preferences -> Custom Styles -> MCP Tools.
- Skills are either Capability Uplift (grant new tools) or Encoded Preference (behaviour patterns, SKILL.md only).
- Recommended workflow: prototype in claude.ai -> implement in Claude Code -> persist decisions to CLAUDE.md.
- LLM coding behavioural guidelines (Karpathy's CLAUDE.md): think first, minimum viable code, surgical changes, goal-driven execution.
- Karpathy's LLM Wiki gist is a reference resource on language model concepts.
- Structured documentation (ADR, PRD, BDD) is the primary control surface for autonomous AI agents.
- Being AI-native is about workflow readiness and context accessibility, not doing everything with AI.
- Sanity's MCP-based "Content OS" strategy: AI agents read/write directly against a defined schema.
- Human-in-the-loop pattern: automated agent action into staging, human reviews and publishes.
- KPI for AI-tooling adoption: ratio of agent/programmatic mutations vs manual UI mutations, paired with error rate.
- CLAUDE.md as a personal profile describing who you are, not just a project.
- Giving an AI an identity shifts instruction-giving into genuine conversation.
- Memory tracking builds a longitudinal self-knowledge layer over time.
- Morning skill pattern flags gaps between stated priorities and actual time allocation.
- Build your AI system from the inside out, from your own thinking style.
- The "staying human" frame produces different AI systems than optimising for speed.
- Taxonomy as a JSON file anchors agent prompts on the right domain meaning.
- Two-agent architecture: monitoring/ingestion agent + deep-research/maintenance agent.
- Knowledge curation loop: agents must actively curate, validate, and maintain relevance.
- Budget-constrained autonomous agent execution with tiered model selection (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus).
- Source validation protocol before storing any insight (reachability, hallucination, paywall, claim check).
- Temperature tagging for knowledge freshness by review cadence.
- Knowledge graph over flat rows: typed relationship edges enable graph traversal.
- Self-improving knowledge gap loop: system identifies gaps and fires new research.
- AI as a personal and organisational capability multiplier.
- Company brain via shared ontology bridges Conway's Law silos.
- SaaS shifting from ready-built software to composable lego pieces.
- Role-specific AI skill map for PMs: research synthesis, competitive intel, predictive analytics, roadmap prioritisation, prototype generation, A/B testing, PRD generation.
- MASTRA: TypeScript-native, open-source agent framework distinguishing autonomous agents from deterministic workflows.
- Unified model router (MASTRA) makes provider swaps config changes.
- Framework-as-library model: MASTRA is imported directly into your app.
- Temporal is a durable-execution platform: persists an immutable Event History and replays on recovery.
- Temporal's determinism split maps onto agent loops: workflow = orchestration, activity = non-deterministic work unit.
- Choosing an orchestration substrate (Temporal vs Conductor-style DSLs) is a real architectural decision.

## Summary
The architecture topic covers three threads: (1) structural and behavioural design principles for software systems built with or guided by LLMs; (2) concrete API architecture patterns, specifically the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern; and (3) real-world examples of CQRS and knowledge-system architectures enforcing separation of concerns. An organisational systems lens frames the company brain as an architectural pattern. This cycle adds durable execution as a fourth thread: Temporal's event-sourced, crash-resilient orchestration model for AI agent loops.

## Key Insights
- Think before coding: state assumptions, surface tradeoffs, ask when confused.
- Simplicity first: minimum code that solves the problem, no speculative features.
- Surgical changes: touch only what you must, match existing style.
- Goal-driven execution: define success criteria upfront.
- ADR is an enforcement tool: CI pipelines reject commits that violate architectural boundaries.
- PRD + BDD with Cucumber creates a continuous chain from product intent to executable specs.
- Design systems with strict component rules constrain AI-generated UIs.
- BFF pattern adds a client-specific API aggregation layer behind a shared API Gateway.
- Web BFFs return rich data; Mobile BFFs return compact, cached, minimal payloads.
- API Gateway owns cross-cutting concerns; each BFF owns client-specific data shaping.
- CQRS in practice: Sanity separates write path (Postgres ledger) from read path (Elasticsearch index).
- Referential integrity without SQL joins via typed pointer objects.
- Confirmed writes trigger async replication/broadcast to update indexes and invalidate caches.
- Binary payloads go to object storage with CDN transforms; structured text flows through the core pipeline.
- A small JSON taxonomy file acts as a semantic configuration layer for AI agents.
- Two-agent specialisation mirrors microservice decomposition.
- Ontology provides the relational layer that taxonomy alone cannot.
- Active curation is an architectural requirement, not an afterthought.
- Voyage + Supabase as a concrete RAG stack for semantic retrieval.
- Budget-managed agent execution as an architectural boundary on inference tier.
- Knowledge graph as a storage primitive with typed edges as first-class schema citizens.
- Self-improving gap loop as a systemic architectural requirement.
- Company brain as an architectural pattern bridging Conway's Law silos.
- Composable software stacks: architecting for composition as SaaS shifts to primitives.
- Temporal: Temporal Service + Client SDK + Workers, self-hosted or Temporal Cloud.
- Determinism is the core architectural constraint: Workflow code must be deterministic, non-deterministic work pushed into Activities.
- Incremental adoption pattern: embed Temporal Client, extract only long-running processes into Workflows/Activities.
- Temporal maps naturally onto AI agent loops: workflow = deterministic loop, LLM/tool calls = Activities.
- Orchestration-substrate choice (Temporal vs Conductor) is itself an architectural decision.

## Open Questions
None.

- BFF Implementation: Web vs Mobile Response Shaping
- Sanity's Content Lake

## Summary
The product thinking topic captures strategic and philosophical perspectives on AI adoption alongside concrete PM framing for positioning and measuring AI-driven products. Core themes: being AI-native is about workflow readiness; strong PM strategy reframes platforms around ecosystem-wide value with KPIs pairing efficiency against quality/trust; and the design goal chosen for an AI product (staying human vs maximising speed) determines the entire interaction model. A role-specific lens brings concrete AI skill areas PMs are expected to build fluency in.

## Key Insights
- Being AI-native does not mean doing everything with AI; it means structuring workflows so the switch is possible and smooth.
- AI-native readiness involves recording meetings, writing decision documents, capturing context structurally.
- Ask "can this be optimised with AI?" rather than "should we use AI?"
- Market positioning shifts when a category commoditises (Sanity: Headless CMS -> Content OS).
- Effective PM framing treats a platform as an organisation-centric ecosystem.
- Architectural choices can be argued in product terms (Postgres-as-ledger + Elasticsearch-as-index).
- A practical AI-strategy KPI pairs adoption with quality/trust.
- The design north star ("stay human" vs "maximise speed") determines the product.
- Identity as a product feature: naming an AI shifts users from commanding to conversing.
- Personalisation surface: a CLAUDE.md-style personal profile is a high-value configuration surface.
- Taxonomy-driven knowledge management as a low-friction personalisation lever.
- The curation loop as a product responsibility, not an ops afterthought.
- AI as organisational intelligence layer bridging Conway's Law silos.
- SaaS shifting from ready-built software to composable lego pieces.
- Better shared context as an organisational design goal.
- The AI skill gap is the opportunity: fluency in directing AI tools is the differentiating skill.

## Open Questions
None.

- Sanity's Content Lake
- Building a company second brain
- AI as Human Capability Multiplier

bodies.wiki/cloud-infra:
## Summary
The cloud / infra topic is newly seeded by a deep-dive into Sanity's Content Lake infrastructure, which combines managed databases, search indexes, object storage, and CDN edge caching on Google Cloud to power a CQRS content platform.

## Key Insights
- Write path: PostgreSQL on GCE acts as the immutable, append-only source-of-truth ledger.
- Read path: Elasticsearch serves all queries via an inverted index; Postgres is never woken for reads.
- Sync/propagation: GKE compute layer replicates Postgres writes to Elasticsearch and broadcasts via Pub/Sub.
- Binary assets are offloaded to GCS buckets with lightweight reference pointers.
- On-the-fly asset transforms handled by a serverless image-processing microservice at the CDN edge.

## Open Questions
None.

## Sources
- Sanity's Content Lake

bodies.notes/claude-code-mcp-three-scope-levels:
### claude.ai MCP
Added in the UI; applies globally across all chats and projects, separate from Claude Code.

### Claude Code MCP -- Three Scopes
- `-scope user` -- Available globally across all projects. Use for servers you always want everywhere (e.g., GitHub, search tools).
- `-scope local` -- Per-user, per-project. The default scope when none is specified.
- `-scope project` -- Writes to `.mcp.json` in the project root. Shared via git.

### Config Storage
- `local` and `user` scopes: Both store in `~/.claude.json` -- local is keyed by project path, user is global.
- `project` scope: Stores in `.mcp.json` at the project root; committable to git for team sharing.

bodies.notes/llm-agent-coding-behavioral-guidel:

## 1. Think Before Coding
Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.

## 2. Simplicity First
Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.

## 3. Surgical Changes

bodies.notes/claude-customization-layers-from-s:

Customization hierarchy: System Prompt (API-level) -> Project Instructions -> User Preferences -> Custom Styles -> MCP Tools

## System Prompt

## Project Instructions
Used in claude.ai projects as persistent context.

bodies.notes/claude-skill-system-skill-md-forma:
Skill format is common to both claude.ai and Claude Code, using a SKILL.md file.

Types of skills:

bodies.notes/claude-prototyping-to-production-w:
## Prototyping vs Building
Use claude.ai for concept and prototype, Claude Code locally for writing code.

Three distinct layers: RUNTIME (API system field), DEVELOPMENT (CLAUDE.md), PROTOTYPING (Project instructions in claude.ai).

## Recommended Workflow

2. DISTILL after each session into CLAUDE.md
3. CODE with Claude Code
4. SYNC back to claude.ai Project

bodies.notes/structured-documentation-for-ai-as:
Source: BDD, ADR, PRD, WTF: Capturing Decisions for Humans and AI Alike -- Michal Cichra, Safe Intelligence

## Core problem: limited context
Both humans and LLMs suffer from limited context. AI agents need explicit, structured documentation to navigate, write, and safely test code.

## Formats for capturing decisions
- ADR: documents why an architectural choice was made and how to enforce it.
- PRD: tracks why a feature exists and the user's journey.
- BDD with Cucumber: bridges PRDs and working code in human-readable form.

## Constraining AI in UI design
Adopt strict design systems and pattern libraries with rigid rules.

## Enforcement loop (Git hooks + CI)
CI pipelines check compliance; violating commits are rejected and linked back to the relevant ADR/PRD.

## Key takeaway
Documentation is not overhead; it is the control surface for autonomous AI agents.
bodies.notes/being-ai-native-means-workflow-rea:
What is AI Native? It doesn't mean making everything with AI. It's about making your workflow ready for the switch -- being conscious of AI tools, improving workflow to provide the right context, connecting parts so AI can have programmatic access.

That could mean recording meetings, writing decision documents, and writing things down.

Ask "can this be optimised with AI?" rather than assuming AI-first. Evaluate AI fairly as part of the technology stack; if it doesn't give good enough results, don't use it.
bodies.notes/bff-architecture-pattern-client-sp:
The Backend for Frontend (BFF) pattern introduces a dedicated API aggregation layer tailored per client type (web, mobile), sitting behind a shared API Gateway and in front of core backend microservices.

## Architecture overview
Clients -> BFF (client-specific) -> API Gateway (shared middleware) -> Core Backend Services -> Database + Cache

- Web BFF: full data, pagination metadata, SEO fields, recommendations, wishlist integration
- Mobile BFF: compact JSON, Redis-cached data, offline support, minimal fields

## Separation of concerns
API Gateway owns authentication, rate limiting, logging/tracing; BFF owns data shaping, service aggregation, client awareness.
bodies.notes/bff-implementation-web-vs-mobile-r:
Concrete code patterns for implementing the BFF architecture, showing how a shared endpoint serves different clients with different response shapes.

Web BFF (Node.js/Express) aggregates from multiple services and enriches the response for web consumers (products + reviews + wishlist + recommendations + SEO metadata + pagination).

Mobile BFF serves the same endpoint with Redis caching and a minimal response shape (id, name, price).

API Gateway middleware (NGINX) routes mobile user-agents to the mobile BFF and all others to the web BFF, while enforcing auth, rate limits, and compression uniformly.
bodies.notes/sanity-s-content-lake-cqrs-archite:
Interview prep briefing for a PM interviewing for Sanity's Content Lake / Content Platform domain.

## 1. Executive Summary & Market Positioning
Sanity is moving from "Headless CMS" to a "Content Operating System for the AI Era" via Sanity Canvas, native Automation (Functions), and AI Native Structuring via MCP.

## 2. Technical Architecture: The Content Lake
Schema-less core with referential integrity via typed pointers. CQRS: write path uses Postgres on GCE as an append-only ledger; read path uses Elasticsearch, never waking Postgres for reads. Sync via GKE + Pub/Sub.

## 3. Asset Pipeline
Text via the core JSON/Elasticsearch pipeline (Portable Text); binary assets to Google Cloud Storage with metadata extraction and on-the-fly CDN transforms.

## 4. Human-in-the-Loop AI
Example: automated translation into a staging area (Content Releases), reviewed and published by a human gatekeeper.

## 5. Interview Q&A framing
Covers ecosystem-centric platform prioritisation, Postgres+Elasticsearch vs MongoDB tradeoffs, and KPI framing (programmatic vs manual mutation ratio, paired with error rate).
bodies.notes/building-a-company-second-brain-ta:
Key insight from a talk on structuring company knowledge for AI agents.

## The problem
Most knowledge lives in agent threads, Atlassian products, or Drive folders -- never becomes shared, maintained insight.

## Core concepts
Taxonomy as a JSON file: define the domain in structured taxonomy, inject into agent prompts to focus meaning.
Ontology matters: build a knowledge graph, not just a document store.
Two-agent architecture: Pulse (daily news) and Scalchi (deep research + maintenance).
Knowledge curation loop: agents must actively curate, validate, and maintain relevance.

## Key takeaway
A tiny JSON taxonomy file + structured agent roles dramatically improves signal-to-noise when using AI over a company's knowledge base.
bodies.notes/building-a-personal-ai-thinking-pa:
Insight from a talk by someone who built their own personal AI system (named Pippi) from scratch.

## Learning approach
Used Claude to learn about Claude; replicated others' workflows early, then decided to build from the inside out.

## What they actually optimised for
Not speed or productivity -- how to stay human in interactions with AI, maintaining judgment and staying in the lead.

## Mechanisms
Writing/blogging as a forcing function; token limits as a forcing function to reconnect with the real world; CLAUDE.md as a personal profile describing who you are.

## Key takeaway
The "stay human" / "build from the inside out" frame produces fundamentally different AI systems than optimising for speed.
bodies.notes/knowledge-graph-architecture-for-c:
Continuation of a talk on building a company AI brain (Data Mobility). Focuses on graph-structured knowledge and self-improvement.

## Graph over rows
Knowledge stored as nodes with typed relationships, not isolated entries. Queries return semantic clusters.

## Self-improving loop
Build summary -> flag gaps -> fire new research -> repeat, evolving without explicit user direction.

## Five takeaways for replication
Taxonomy first; simple continuous agents; structured storage (Voyage + Supabase); MCP access for agents; self-evolving design.
bodies.notes/company-ai-knowledge-agent-multi-a:
A mobility data company describes their two-agent AI knowledge system.

## Agents
Pulse (news scout, ingests 44 newsletters nightly) and Research agent/Scalchi (validates sources, populates the knowledge base).

## Source validation protocol
Checks URL reachability, hallucination, paywall access, and claim accuracy.

## Budget and model mix
$20/day autonomous, $100+/day user-directed; Haiku/Sonnet/Opus tiered by task.

## Temperature tagging
Insights tagged with review cadence (daily for breaking stories, 6 months for stable regulation).

## Storage
RAG with Voyage embeddings + Supabase. Slack integration makes capture ambient.
bodies.notes/personal-ai-thinking-partner-claud:
A talk by the creator of the "Pippi" personal AI system. Core thesis: optimise for staying human and keeping judgment in the lead.

## CLAUDE.md as self-portrait
Describe you -- how you think, communication style, correction patterns -- as an evolving mirror of cognitive style.

## Key skills
GrowthMD (tough-love reflection), LoveMD (celebrates growth), Morning skill (flags misalignment between priorities and time use).

## Named AI identity (Pippi)
Giving the AI a name shifts the dynamic from instructions to conversation.

## Mindprint starter guide
13 reflective questions generate a personalised CLAUDE.md, with fresh-start and cognitive-layer tracks.

## Meta-insight
Repeated personalised AI use teaches you about your own thinking and decision-making.

bodies.notes/mastra-typescript-native-ai-agent-:
MASTRA is an open-source TypeScript framework for building AI agents, created by the Gatsby team. Graduated Y Combinator (W25, $13M), hit v1.0 January 2026.

## Core Architecture
createAgent (autonomous), createTool, createWorkflow (deterministic pipelines).

## Key Features
Model router across dozens of providers; observational memory; guardrails; native MCP support; Mastra Studio.

## Framework Model
It's a library you import, not a SaaS service -- you own the infrastructure.

## Licensing & Cost
Apache 2.0, free framework, pay LLM providers directly.

## Adoption
Used by Replit, SoftBank, PayPal, PLAID, Marsh McLennan.
bodies.notes/temporal-durable-execution-for-ai-:
Temporal is a durable-execution platform guaranteeing workflow completion after crashes, outages, or failures via an immutable Event History and automatic replay.

## Architecture
Temporal Service (backend), Temporal Client (SDK, embedded in your app), Workers (execute workflow + activity code in your infra).

## Execution Model
Workflows: deterministic orchestration logic. Activities: non-deterministic work units (LLM calls, API calls, DB queries), retryable, results cached in Event History.

## AI Agent Orchestration
Workflow = deterministic loop/decision structure; Activities = LLM calls + tool invocations -- durability across crashes, no re-paying for completed LLM calls.

## Temporal vs Conductor
Temporal: code-first, tight orchestration/business-logic coupling, natural for agent loops. Conductor: declarative DSL, orchestration separated from services, better for polyglot microservice coordination.

bodies.questions/what-are-the-key-goals-and-wor:
Suggested answer -- synthesised from notes: Four Ways to Use Claude, Claude Customization Layers, Claude Prototyping-to-Production Workflow.

Claude supports four distinct usage modes: (1) end user -- chat interface for goals like planning or learning; (2) builder with Claude Code -- Claude as development partner; (3) API builder -- custom applications via the Claude API; (4) automation -- recurring workflows via Claude Code or extensions.

Effective use requires customisation at the right layer: System Prompt for API-level control; Project Instructions in claude.ai for persistent project context; User Preferences for account-wide defaults; MCP Tools and Skills for capability extension.

Recommended workflow: prototype in claude.ai using Project Instructions as a scratchpad, then transition to Claude Code for implementation using CLAUDE.md for project-level context.
